timeBasis.note: Retrospective FY2025 review: uses the FY2025 10-K (27 Oct 2025) and the FY2026 guidance (22 Oct 2025), which were published after the price date.

notChanged: Sales-to-capital stays at 2.0 in all scenarios (Input sheet!B31, B32).
Terminal tax rate stays at 25% (Input sheet!B24).
The FY2025 R&D capitalization adjustment ($2.27m) is added to guided operating income in every scenario; using the same amount in FY2026 is an assumption.
Expected proceeds from the Americas homecare sale are not added because no price was disclosed and the sale had not closed.

bear.label: Bear
rationale: Year-1 revenue at the low end of FY2026 guidance ($630m on the pro forma base). Years 2-5 grow 3.25% a year, the compound rate of a regional build: Americas 2%, EIMEA 4%, Asia-Pacific 5% (FY2025 segment growth was 3.1%, 7.0% and 6.1%).
Year-1 margin from the low end of guidance ($103m operating income on $630m of sales) plus the workbook's R&D adjustment, held flat; reported operating margin averaged 16.6% in FY2022-FY2025.

Cost of capital from the Household Products unlevered beta and Damodaran's smoothed ERP (5.37%, the ten-year average implied premium, measured against the T-bond rate). It drifts to the market's cost of capital, 9.45%, by year 10.
No excess returns on new capital after year 10 (terminal ROIC equals terminal WACC). Terminal growth 2.0%.

base.label: Base
rationale: Year-1 revenue at the midpoint of FY2026 guidance ($642.5m on the pro forma base, which leaves out the homecare brands held for sale). Years 2-5 grow 5.81% a year, the compound rate of a regional build: Americas 4%, EIMEA 7%, Asia-Pacific 8% (FY2025 segment growth was 3.1%, 7.0% and 6.1%).

Year-1 margin from the guidance midpoint ($106.5m operating income on $642.5m of sales) plus the workbook's R&D adjustment. The 18% target by year 5 is an analyst assumption; reported operating margin averaged 16.6% in FY2022-FY2025 and 19.4% in FY2017-FY2020.

Cost of capital from a bottom-up beta (average of Damodaran's Chemical (Specialty) and Household Products unlevered betas, January 2025) relevered at WD-40's market debt-to-equity, the 29 Aug 2025 10-year Treasury yield and Damodaran's September 2025 implied ERP. Held flat because WD-40 is already a mature company.
New capital after year 10 earns 15%, above the cost of capital because the brand and distribution persist, and well below the 27% or so the Base case earns in years 1-10. Terminal growth 2.5%.

bull.label: Bull
rationale: Year-1 revenue at the top of FY2026 guidance ($655m on the pro forma base). Years 2-5 grow 7.98% a year, the compound rate of a regional build: Americas 6%, EIMEA 9%, Asia-Pacific 11% (FY2025 segment growth was 3.1%, 7.0% and 6.1%).

Year-1 margin from the top of guidance ($110m operating income on $655m of sales) plus the workbook's R&D adjustment. The 20% target by year 5 is an analyst assumption near the 19.4% reported FY2017-FY2020 average.
Cost of capital from the Blume-adjusted 5-year weekly regression beta and Damodaran's sustainable-payout ERP (3.68%, measured against the T-bond rate).
New capital after year 10 earns 20%. Terminal growth 3.0%, below the 4.23% risk-free rate.
